items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Rodger said... he wanted to form an orchestra with my co-operation. We were still working on the project while I was gigging with Fats

ctx.x: We played this town for three days. He would invite the musicians to drink with him, but he drank most of the gallon.

When I was working at the Ubangi Club with Leon Abbey, a fellow named Rodger Kramer arrived in New York from Egypt and came to see me at the club. I had met his brother Leon Kramer in Alexandria, but Rodger said he had been in France singing with Arthur Briggs, having arrived in France about the same time as I arrived in Egypt. He said that he was going to change his name from Kramer to Ray and he wanted to form an orchestra with my co-operation.

We were still working on the project while I was gigging with Fats and in July I was contacted to replace a trumpet player in Noble Sissle's orchestra who had joined a U.S. Navy Band. And again the first appearance with the orchestra was at the Howard Theatre in Washington D.C. There were two things that were different however, with playing the Howard with Andy Kirk and the same theatre a few months later with Noble Sissle. First the band didn't swing and secondly, I did not drink the way I had when I went there…
